what_it_does: mLR accelerates image reconstruction using a technique called Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers with Fast Fourier Transform (ADMM-FFT). The problem is that laminography (a 3D imaging technique) reconstruction is very slow and uses lots of memory because the same Fourier transform operations get repeated many times. mLR notices when the same operations repeat and caches their results instead of recomputing them, dramatically speeding up the process. The approach also saves CPU memory by moving data between CPU and GPU intelligently, and can run this across multiple GPUs on single or multiple machines to handle large datasets.
